- Differences in DPI between `window_set_window_buttons_offset and window_get_safe_title_margins`.
- `WINDOW_EVENT_TITLEBAR_CHANGE` call.
- And incorrect `set_custom_minimum_size`.

So if all three of other suggested changes are applied, it will no longer freeze and seems to be working fine without it.

Fixed!

I attempted to implement this, thanks for the link. It seems to be a fairly deep Win32/DWM mess.

Returning `HTMAXBUTTON` for our custom maximize button does make Windows treat that area as non-client input, but the Snap Layout popup still only appears over DWM’s internal caption-button bounds. Those bounds can be queried using `DWMWA_CAPTION_BUTTON_BOUNDS`, but they are read-only and do not necessarily match Godot’s custom button geometry.

I found one way to make the popup follow our custom `HTMAXBUTTON` region: suppress native non-client activation/painting (`WM_NCACTIVATE`/`WM_NCPAINT`). Unfortunately, suppressing `WM_NCPAINT` also removes the standard DWM window shadow. Forwarding that message to either `DefWindowProcW` or `DwmDefWindowProc` restores the shadow, but also restores DWM’s internal caption-button behavior, so the popup again appears only within DWM’s own maximize-button region.

I also tried DWM frame margins, `DWMNCRP_ENABLED`, explicit non-client message forwarding, manifest compatibility declarations, and `CS_DROPSHADOW`. Nothing preserved both arbitrary custom caption-button geometry and the normal Windows 11 shadow. `CS_DROPSHADOW` only produced the obsolete 1-pixel legacy shadow.

You can actually observe this in the Windows Terminal app too - hover your mouse in the bottom ~20% of the maximize icon, and notice that the snap overlay does not appear :)

My opinion is this is not worth implementing.
